predecessors.name: Afsharid Iran
predecessors.text: Kandahar, where Ahmad Shah was crowned on 23 July 1747, and Ghazni, taken 'with little opposition'

predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: Kabul (October 1747) and Peshawar (1747-48), taken from the Mughal-appointed governor Nasir Khan; the Punjab, Multan and Kashmir followed in 1752

successors.name: Emirate of Afghanistan
successors.text: the Principality of Kabul: 'The Sadozai rulers controlled little more than Kabul and its surroundings within about 160 km by 1818'; the Barakzai superseded the Durrani at Kabul in March 1823

successors.name: Principality of Kandahar
successors.text: Kandahar, founded by Sher Dil Khan in August 1818 'as a breakaway from the Durrani Empire'

successors.name: Principality of Herat
successors.text: Herat, held by the Sadozai Mahmud Shah and Kamran Shah from 1818; the page lists the Kingdom of Herat among the Durrani successors

successors.name: Sikh Empire
successors.text: Multan (1818), the Kashmir Valley (1819) and the Peshawar valley as a tributary (1823)

ledger.x: 1747: Ahmad Shah Durrani is crowned at Kandahar.
October 1747: Kabul is handed over.
1748: Peshawar falls.
January 1748: the first Afghan campaign into the Punjab.
1749: Sindh enters Afghan suzerainty.
Late 1750: Herat falls after a long siege.
November 1750: the first siege of Mashhad.
1752: Kashmir.
Summer 1752: the northern Uzbek khanate.
By summer 1752: Balkh passes from the Qataghanids to Hajji Bi under Ahmad Shah.
3 April 1752: the Punjab passes to the Afghans.
3 April 1752: the Punjab, Multan and Lahore to Sirhind.
1753: Badakhshan is subjugated.
1 December 1754: Mashhad surrenders.
9 May 1755: Shahrokh Shah is restored at Mashhad 'as a Durrani protectorate'.
17 June 1755: Nishapur submits.

1758: Kalat. After besieging Kalat for forty days Ahmad Shah 'reaffirmed Nasir Khan in his position' under a treaty requiring recognition of his suzerainty. The Kalat page says accounts conflict: 'Since 1748, Kalat was a vassal state of Durrani Empire', 'Kalat did not pay any tribute to Durrani Empire thereafter', and…
1759: the Afghans reach Lahore to meet the Marathas.
14 January 1761: Panipat.
1762: the Sikh war.
1763: Ahmad Shah 'occupied the regions between Tashkent and Kokand, withdrawing by 1764'.
1764: the Afghans withdraw from the Tashkent-Kokand lands ('withdrawing by 1764').
1767: the last of Ahmad Shah's Indian invasions.
1768: Shah Murad Manghit of Bukhara invades.
1768: Shah Murad negotiates and 'recognized Afghan control over Balkh'.
1769 or 1770: Badakhshan is occupied.
1769 or 1770: Badakhshan is annexed after Sultan Shah's execution; Sultan Shah had sought Qing help after the 1759 pressure.
1772: the eastern Punjab goes to the Sikhs.
1776: the capital moves from Kandahar to Kabul, with Peshawar as winter capital (infobox 'Kandahar (1747-1776); Kabul (1776-1823); Peshawar as winter capital (1776-1823)').
1783: the Kalhora dynasty falls.
1783: the Talpurs rule Sindh as tributaries.
After 1783: Azad Khan, governor of Kashmir, 'rebelled after 1783 and stopped sending revenue to Kabul'.
11 December 1786: the Kashmir rebellion ends and 'Kashmir was reabsorbed under firm imperial control'.
May 1793: Humayun Mirza rebels at Kandahar against Zaman Shah ('Humayun Shah (rival, Kandahar): May 1793 - Dec 1795'); the civil war began on 20 May 1793.
December 1795: Humayun is defeated at Qalati Ghilji and flees; Zaman Shah later had him executed.
1796: Mashhad falls to the Qajar.
1796: Nishapur goes with Mashhad in the Qajar conquest of Khorasan.
1818: Herat becomes the seat of Mahmud Shah and Kamran Shah.
1818: Multan.
1818: Kalat's tribute passes from the Durrani throne to the new Principality of Kandahar.
1818: Sindh's tribute passes from the Durrani throne to the new Principality of Kandahar.
August 1818: Kandahar breaks away.
3 July 1819: Shopian.
1823: the Maimana Khanate passes to the Barakzai orbit; the Emirate page lists the Maimana Khanate among the Emirate's predecessors.
14 March 1823: Nowshera.
March 1823: the Durrani Empire ends at Kabul.

wars.name: Durrani invasions of the Punjab (Mughal campaigns)
wars.outcome: Durrani victory: the treaty of 3 April 1752 annexed the Punjab with Multan and Lahore to Sirhind and Kashmir followed.

wars.name: Durrani campaigns in Khorasan
wars.outcome: Herat fell in late 1750; Mashhad surrendered on 1 December 1754 and Shahrokh Shah was restored on 9 May 1755 as a Durrani protectorate; Nishapur submitted on 17 June 1755 and its ruler Abbas Quli stayed on as governor (a vassal, not a conquest).

wars.name: Durrani conquest of Afghan Turkestan
wars.outcome: Balkh taken back from the Qataghanids under Hajji Bi as Ahmad Shah's governor (summer 1752), Badakhshan subjugated (1753), Bukharans pushed back across the Amu Darya (1761), Balkh recognised as Afghan by Shah Murad (1768), Badakhshan occupied (1769).

wars.name: Siege of Kalat (1758)
wars.outcome: Ahmad Shah besieged Kalat for over forty days, failed to storm it, and 'reaffirmed Nasir Khan in his position' under a treaty of suzerainty; the Kalat page says Kalat paid no tribute afterwards.

wars.name: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Durrani victory on 14 January 1761; the Punjab and Kashmir stayed Afghan.

wars.name: Durrani-Sikh wars (1762-1767)
wars.outcome: The Vadda Ghallughara (1762) and the invasions of 1764-65 and 1766-67 did not hold the Punjab; by 1772 'he had lost parts of Punjab to the Sikhs'.

wars.name: Azad Khan's revolt in Kashmir
wars.outcome: The governor Azad Khan stopped sending revenue after 1783; the revolt ended on 11 December 1786 and Kashmir was reabsorbed.

wars.name: Durrani civil war (Zaman Shah to Ayub Shah)
wars.outcome: Humayun's revolt at Kandahar (May 1793 to December 1795), Zaman Shah's overthrow by Mahmud Shah (25 July 1801), and the reigns of Shuja, Mahmud, Ali and Ayub ended with the breakup of 1818.

wars.name: Qajar conquest of Khorasan (1796)
wars.outcome: Agha Mohammad Shah took Mashhad and Shahrokh Shah died in 1796; the Durrani protectorate over Khorasan ended.

wars.name: Afghan-Sikh wars (1818-1823)
wars.outcome: Sikh victories: Multan (1818), Kashmir at Shopian (3 July 1819), Nowshera (14 March 1823) leaving Peshawar tributary.
